name: Perfect Derma peel
lead: The Perfect Derma Peel, also sold as the Perfect Peel, is a branded chemical peel performed by trained providers in clinics and med spas. Providers describe it as a blend of trichloroacetic acid (TCA), phenol, retinoic acid, salicylic acid, kojic acid, glutathione and vitamin C, and promote it for fine lines, acne scarring, melasma and dull skin, with the aim of a smoother, brighter, more even complexion [2].

A session takes about 30 minutes in clinic, followed by peeling that Elite Aesthetics says lasts 5-7 days, with days three and four the most intense [2]. Medium-depth peels in general cause a controlled injury to the skin that is followed by shedding and renewal [1].
The brand-specific claims come from the manufacturer and the clinics that sell it; no independent clinical trial of this blend was found.

chain: Acid blend causes a controlled exfoliation
Skin sheds over several days and renews
angle.text: A provider applies the peel to the face and the skin darkens and flakes over about a week; users are aiming for more even tone, less pigmentation, softer fine lines and smoother acne-scarred skin. A course of treatments is typically described rather than a single session [2].

infobox: Branded chemical peel (described as medium depth)
TCA, phenol, retinoic acid, salicylic acid, kojic acid, glutathione, vitamin C (provider descriptions) [2]
Pigmentation, melasma, acne scars, fine lines [2]

paras: Elite Aesthetics lists TCA as the 'gold-standard' peel ingredient that removes dead and damaged skin cells, retinoic acid as stimulating cell renewal, salicylic acid as clearing oily skin and acne, phenol as an exfoliant, kojic acid as brightening pigmentation, glutathione as an antioxidant said to reduce melasma by inhibiting melanin production, and vitamin C with other nutrients as supporting collagen [2].
Wikipedia describes peels as acids that injure the outer layers of skin in a controlled way so that it peels and regrows, with TCA a classic medium-depth agent [1].

Elite Aesthetics says the treatment takes about 30 minutes, is described as painless apart from light tingling, and is followed by 5-7 days of peeling; normal routines can continue, makeup is avoided for the first few days, and a home pack with retinol wipes and a vitamin C moisturiser is provided [2]. The clinic advises not picking at peeling skin [2].

Encyclopedic sources note that the deeper a peel, the more complications can arise, including photosensitivity, prolonged redness, pigment changes, milia, skin thinning and scarring, and that medium-depth peels are performed by medical providers [1]. Discomfort such as warmth or burning during application is common with TCA [1]. Sun protection and provider aftercare instructions are standard parts of peel care.
Peels like this are discussed in looksmaxxing circles under skin-quality work, alongside tretinoin and microneedling, as a professional option for tone and scarring.
No studies found. Research on medium-depth TCA peels as a category exists, but no trial of this specific blend was found.

card.summary: A branded medium-depth acid peel done by providers, aimed at evening skin tone, pigmentation, fine lines and acne scars.
card.note: Medium-depth peels can cause pigment changes, prolonged redness or scarring; done by trained providers.

quick.overview:
The Perfect Derma Peel is a branded medium-depth chemical peel offered by clinics. It is promoted for smoother, brighter, more even skin and for acne scars and pigmentation.

It is usually described as a course of treatments, each followed by several days of visible peeling.
quick.mechanism: A blend of acids, including TCA, causes controlled exfoliation, after which new skin forms. Other included agents are described as targeting pigment and adding antioxidants.
quick.risks: Medium-depth peels can cause prolonged redness, pigment changes, sun sensitivity and, rarely, scarring. They are performed by trained providers.
